batches.acceptance: SC1, SC2, SC3, SC4. Build clean. Read-only: writes nothing to Confluence and nothing to state.
batches.boundary: Reports the shape. Changes no page and moves nothing.

test_manifest.assertion: Every directory with publishable pages and no index is named, with page count and resolved ancestor.
Parents wider than maxChildren are named, root included; default 12.
structure check emitted; findings on StatusReport.Structure; produced with no probes run.
maxChildren absent → 12; present → honoured; schema accepts it.
movedFrom on a live entry → Move, state rekeyed with every field carried, old path absent from PrunePlan.
Tombstone written; a second identical run is a no-op; rebuild-state does not adopt it.
A link to a moved page's old path resolves to the new page.
Five ambiguous claims throw with paths named; an unresolvable movedFrom warns and plans Create.
Title changed, body unchanged → Move, new title written, approval survives.
docs-restructure registered and well-formed; docs-loop's exclusion points at it.

out_of_scope: Synthesizing index pages — PageHierarchy's refusal stands.
wiki.structure declared taxonomy in docume.json — belongs in the consumer's _meta/STYLE.md (rule §9.5).
order: frontmatter for path-independent sibling ordering — separate spec.
Git rename detection — GitRepository passes --no-renames deliberately.
Mass in-tree link rewriting on a move — the tombstone covers correctness.
Deleting tombstones — a verb that removes identity records needs --prune-grade care.
Failing a build on structure findings — Warning, with --json for repos that want to gate.
The AurServices content work: 17 index pages and the business-tier regrouping are that repo's PRs.
assumptions: The Confluence move API repositions without renaming, so a title change is a titled update against the same id.
A page's sealed verdict is bound to content and sources, not path, so a rekey carries it correctly.
wiki.homePage stays one index name applied per directory; per-directory overrides are not contemplated.
Reparenting notifies watchers once per moved page; the AurServices Phase 1 run accepts that cost deliberately.

risks.risk: movedFrom consumed after PrunePlanner reads state would present the old path as an orphan; a --prune in the same session trashes the page the move was meant to preserve.
risks.mitigation: Plan-time ordering invariant with a dedicated asserting test, not a comment.

risks.risk: Reparenting 70 AurServices pages fires a watcher notification each.
risks.mitigation: One deliberate publish rather than a drip; called out in the Phase 1 PR body.

risks.risk: wide-parent's threshold of 12 is a guess and may nag.
risks.mitigation: Configurable, Warning-level; a bad default costs one line in docume.json.

risks.risk: A crafted movedFrom transfers an approved page's id to new content.
risks.mitigation: A new body moves the content hash and InvalidatesApproval strips the label (§6.2 step 7); the five hard errors keep any transfer from being silent.

delta.driver: AurServices Confluence cutover 2026-09-02: 146 pages published, every check green, 54 on the space root.

amendments.driver: gpt-5.6-sol review of PR #13 flagged the intermediate-directory case as an SC1 gap.
amendments.change: orphaned-directory means a directory with publishable pages BENEATH it and no index page, not only one holding pages directly. The finding gains directPageCount alongside pageCount, and resolvedParent is computed for the directory's would-be index page rather than read off one of its pages.
amendments.why: The narrow reading let the check fall silent on a tree that still skipped levels: report a/b only, somebody writes a/b/README.md, and the check goes quiet while that index still hangs two levels up. Identical output on the AurServices tree; the difference shows only in nested trees.
